objects.description: Enumeration of error/status codes returned by the rwpng API for reading and writing PNG files. Values indicate various failure conditions or success.
Packed 8-bit-per-channel RGBA color struct used for palettes or pixel data. Fields r, g, b, a are in that order.

Linked-list node representing an ancillary PNG chunk preserved when reading/writing. Holds chunk payload, size, 4-byte name plus NUL, and a location tag. Lifetime is managed by the owning image structs.
Enumeration describing how color space/metadata is handled for input/output PNGs (e.g., sRGB, ICC profile, gAMA/cHRM). Used to record or control color transforms.

Container for 24/32-bit (RGBA) PNG image data as read/written by rwpng. Holds dimensions, file size, gamma, row pointers, contiguous RGBA buffer, preserved chunks list, and color transform metadata. jmpbuf is for error handling. Memory for buffers/chunks is owned by this struct and should be released with rwpng_free_image24.

Container for 8-bit indexed PNG images. Holds dimensions, file size limits, gamma, row pointers, indexed pixel data, preserved chunks, palette (up to 256 RGBA entries), color transform, and a fast compression flag. jmpbuf is for error handling. Resources should be released with rwpng_free_image8.
Union that can represent either a png24_image or png8_image and shares a jmp_buf for error handling. Useful for generic handling where the exact format varies.

functions.name: rwpng_version_info
functions.description: Writes library/version information to the provided FILE stream. Typical usage is to print version info to stdout or a log before processing images. Exact output format is unspecified.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open FILE* suitable for writing (e.g., stdout, stderr, or a writable file).
The stream should be opened in a mode that allows writing text.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown.

functions.name: rwpng_read_image24
functions.signature: pngquant_error rwpng_read_image24(FILE *infile, png24_image *mainprog_ptr, int strip, int verbose);
functions.description: Reads a PNG image from infile into a 24/32-bit image container (png24_image). On success, mainprog_ptr is populated with image dimensions, metadata, and pixel data (rgba_data/row_pointers). The strip parameter likely controls stripping of alpha or metadata; verbose likely increases logging. Returns a pngquant_error code indicating success or the reason of failure.
requirements: infile must be a valid, open FILE* positioned at the beginning of a PNG stream and readable (binary mode recommended).
mainprog_ptr must be non-null and point to a png24_image struct that the function will initialize/populate.
Caller must check the return value; only SUCCESS (0) indicates success; any non-zero pngquant_error indicates failure.
On SUCCESS, the caller is responsible for releasing allocated resources with rwpng_free_image24(mainprog_ptr).
strip and verbose are treated as integer flags; valid values are not documented here; typical usage is 0 (off) or non-zero (on).
Behavior regarding pre-initialized fields of mainprog_ptr is unspecified; callers should not rely on existing contents being preserved.

functions.name: rwpng_write_image8
functions.description: Writes an indexed-color (8-bit) PNG image to outfile using the data and palette contained in png8_image. Returns a pngquant_error indicating success or the reason of failure. Intended for saving paletted images after quantization.
requirements: outfile must be a valid, open FILE* suitable for binary writing and positioned at the desired start location.
mainprog_ptr must be non-null and contain a properly initialized png8_image describing the image to write (dimensions, pixel data, palette, and related fields).
Caller must check the return value; only SUCCESS (0) indicates success.
On success or failure, memory ownership of buffers inside mainprog_ptr remains with the caller; use rwpng_free_image8 when appropriate to free allocations made by the rwpng routines.
num_palette must correspond to the palette entries used; exact constraints are not documented here (typical PNG limit is 256).
Any optional limits (e.g., maximum_file_size) and flags (e.g., fast_compression) should be set by the caller as needed; exact semantics are not specified in this header.

functions.name: rwpng_write_image24
functions.description: Writes a 24/32-bit PNG image to outfile using the pixel data and metadata provided in png24_image. Returns a pngquant_error status. Intended for saving full-color images (e.g., those read via rwpng_read_image24 or prepared by the caller).
requirements: outfile must be a valid, open FILE* suitable for binary writing and positioned at the desired start location.
mainprog_ptr must be non-null and point to a const png24_image with properly initialized dimensions and pixel buffers.
Caller must check the return value; only SUCCESS (0) indicates success.
The function does not take ownership of mainprog_ptr or its buffers; freeing (if needed) remains the caller’s responsibility via rwpng_free_image24 when applicable.

functions.name: rwpng_free_image24
functions.description: Releases memory and resources associated with a png24_image previously populated by rwpng routines. Use after a successful rwpng_read_image24 or after the caller is done with a png24_image created/filled for writing.
requirements: Argument must be either NULL (no-op behavior unknown) or a pointer to a png24_image previously initialized/populated by rwpng functions.
After calling, any internal pointers (e.g., rgba_data, row_pointers, chunks) become invalid; do not access them.
Call exactly once per image allocation to avoid double-free; calling multiple times is unsafe unless explicitly documented (not specified here).

functions.name: rwpng_free_image8
functions.description: Releases memory and resources associated with a png8_image previously populated by rwpng routines. Use after writing or when discarding an image prepared for writing.
requirements: Argument must be either NULL (no-op behavior unknown) or a pointer to a png8_image previously initialized/populated by rwpng functions.
After calling, any internal pointers (e.g., indexed_data, row_pointers, chunks, palette) become invalid; do not access them.
Call exactly once per image allocation to avoid double-free; calling multiple times is unsafe unless explicitly documented (not specified here).

data_types.description: Any sequence of bytes stored in a file. No structure or encoding is assumed; data may be empty or any length. Used when a function opens a FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME and only writes to it (content is irrelevant) or when the filename itself is fuzz-provided but not the data format.

Bytes representing a PNG file stream as defined by the PNG specification (signature, IHDR, IDAT, IEND, etc.). May include valid or invalid PNGs since fuzzing supplies arbitrary content; expected by functions that read PNGs from a file.

An in-memory buffer of arbitrary bytes produced by FUZZ_PARAM_STR, with no required encoding or structure. May be empty; consumers read bytes sequentially as raw entropy (e.g., to fill palettes or pixel buffers).

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary binary file data
# Target stub opens a FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME for writing and then writes version info to it.
# The file contents provided by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME are irrelevant for correctness, but
# some fuzzers may also exercise filename parsing (paths, special chars) or pre-existing
# file contents if opened with different modes in other stubs. We'll generate a small,
# arbitrary, but varied binary buffer that could serve as a file payload. Keep <= 4096 bytes.

_MAGIC_TAGS: List[bytes] = [
    b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n",           # PNG signature
    b"%PDF-1.7\n",                     # PDF header
    b"GIF89a",                          # GIF header
    b"\xff\xd8\xff\xe0JFIF\x00",     # JPEG header
    b"PK\x03\x04",                     # ZIP header
    b"\x7fELF",                         # ELF header
    b"BM",                               # BMP header
    b"OggS\x00\x02",                    # OGG header
    b"ID3",                              # MP3 ID3
]

_TEXT_SNIPPETS: List[bytes] = [
    b"# This is a test file for fuzzing.\n",
    b"version=1.2.3\n",
    b"name=rwpng_fuzz\n",
    b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.\n",
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_arbitrary_file(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide size profile: small, medium, or near limit.
    profile = rng.choices(["small", "medium", "large"], weights=[5, 3, 1], k=1)[0]
    if profile == "small":
        target = rng.randint(0, 256)
    elif profile == "medium":
        target = rng.randint(257, 2048)
    else:
        target = rng.randint(2049, 4096)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Optionally start with a known magic to simulate realistic files.
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        parts.append(rng.choice(_MAGIC_TAGS))

    # Insert some structured-looking fields.
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        # Little-endian 32-bit length + random payload
        payload_len = rng.randint(0, 64)
        parts.append(b"LEN" + struct.pack("<I", payload_len))
        parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, payload_len))

    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        # Key-value text area
        kv_count = rng.randint(1, 5)
        for _ in range(kv_count):
            k = rng.choice([b"alpha", b"beta", b"gamma", b"delta", b"path", b"mode"]) \
                + b"_" + str(rng.randint(0, 999)).encode()
            v = rng.choice(_TEXT_SNIPPETS).strip()
            parts.append(k + b"=" + v + b"\n")

    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Some zeros and 0xFF runs to simulate sparse/binary areas
        parts.append(b"\x00" * rng.randint(0, 64))
        parts.append(b"\xff" * rng.randint(0, 64))

    # Random middle chunk
    parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 512)))

    # Optionally end with newline-terminated text
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(rng.choice(_TEXT_SNIPPETS))

    data = b"".join(parts)

    # Adjust to target size by trimming or padding with random bytes.
    if len(data) > target:
        data = data[:target]
    elif len(data) < target:
        data += _rand_bytes(rng, target - len(data))

    # Ensure we never exceed 4096 bytes
    return data[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """Generate arbitrary binary file data (<=4096 bytes) based on a seed.

    The target fuzzer stub writes to the provided filename, so contents are not
    required to be valid; we still provide varied but benign content to be reused
    by other stubs that may read files.
    """
    return _make_arbitrary_file(seed)

import random
import struct
import zlib
from typing import List, Tuple

# PNG builder to generate valid PNG images with variations to exercise rwpng_read_image24
# Focus: valid PNG files with different color types/bit depths, interlace, ancillary chunks, gamma/sRGB/ICC hints,
# small dimensions to keep under 4096 bytes.

PNG_SIG = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"

# Helpers

def _crc(chunk_type: bytes, data: bytes) -> int:
    return zlib.crc32(chunk_type + data) & 0xffffffff

def _chunk(chunk_type: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + chunk_type + data + struct.pack(">I", _crc(chunk_type, data))

# Color type mapping for IHDR and encoder expectations
# 0: Grayscale, 2: Truecolor, 3: Indexed, 4: Grayscale+Alpha, 6: Truecolor+Alpha


def _ihdr(width: int, height: int, bit_depth: int, color_type: int, interlace: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # Compression method 0, filter method 0
    data = struct.pack(
        ">IIBBBBB",
        width,
        height,
        bit_depth,
        color_type,
        0,
        0,
        interlace,
    )
    return _chunk(b"IHDR", data)


def _plte(palette: List[Tuple[int, int, int]]) -> bytes:
    data = bytes([c for rgb in palette for c in rgb])
    return _chunk(b"PLTE", data)


def _trns_for_palette(alpha: List[int]) -> bytes:
    return _chunk(b"tRNS", bytes(alpha))


def _srgb(intent: int) -> bytes:
    return _chunk(b"sRGB", bytes([intent & 3]))


def _gama(gamma_scaled_100k: int) -> bytes:
    return _chunk(b"gAMA", struct.pack(">I", gamma_scaled_100k))


def _chrm(white_x, white_y, red_x, red_y, green_x, green_y, blue_x, blue_y) -> bytes:
    vals = [white_x, white_y, red_x, red_y, green_x, green_y, blue_x, blue_y]
    data = b"".join(struct.pack(">I", int(v)) for v in vals)
    return _chunk(b"cHRM", data)


def _iCCP(name: str, profile_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    # name: 1-79 bytes, Latin-1, null-terminated
    nm = name.encode("latin1", errors="ignore")[:79]
    data = nm + b"\x00" + b"\x00" + zlib.compress(profile_bytes)
    return _chunk(b"iCCP", data)


def _text(keyword: str, text: str) -> bytes:
    kw = keyword.encode("latin1", errors="ignore")[:79]
    return _chunk(b"tEXt", kw + b"\x00" + text.encode("latin1", errors="ignore"))


def _idat_rows(filtered_rows: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    raw = b"".join(filtered_rows)
    comp = zlib.compress(raw, level=6)
    return _chunk(b"IDAT", comp)


def _iend() -> bytes:
    return _chunk(b"IEND", b"")


def _make_rows(width: int, height: int, bpp: int, color_type: int, bit_depth: int) -> List[bytes]:
    # bpp is bytes per pixel for 8-bit channels; for lower bit depths pack bits accordingly
    rows = []
    if color_type in (0, 3):
        # Grayscale or indexed: bit depths may be 1,2,4,8
        bits_per_sample = bit_depth
        samples_per_byte = 8 // bits_per_sample
        row_samples = width
        row_bytes = (row_samples + samples_per_byte - 1) // samples_per_byte
        for y in range(height):
            # gradient/pattern
            samples = [(x + y) % (1 << bits_per_sample) for x in range(row_samples)]
            # pack bits MSB-first per PNG spec
            b = bytearray(row_bytes)
            idx = 0
            for i, s in enumerate(samples):
                pos = i % samples_per_byte
                shift = (samples_per_byte - 1 - pos) * bits_per_sample
                b[idx] |= (s & ((1 << bits_per_sample) - 1)) << shift
                if pos == samples_per_byte - 1:
                    idx += 1
            # filter type 0 (None)
            rows.append(b"\x00" + bytes(b))
        return rows
    else:
        # 8-bit per component paths (bit_depth 8)
        for y in range(height):
            row = bytearray(width * bpp)
            for x in range(width):
                if color_type == 2:  # RGB
                    r = (x * 17 + y * 29) & 0xFF
                    g = (x * 37 + y * 13) & 0xFF
                    b = (x * 7 + y * 53) & 0xFF
                    o = x * 3
                    row[o:o+3] = bytes((r, g, b))
                elif color_type == 4:  # Gray+Alpha
                    g = (x * 23 + y * 11) & 0xFF
                    a = (255 - ((x * 41 + y * 19) & 0xFF))
                    o = x * 2
                    row[o:o+2] = bytes((g, a))
                elif color_type == 6:  # RGBA
                    r = (x * 17 + y * 29) & 0xFF
                    g = (x * 37 + y * 13) & 0xFF
                    b = (x * 7 + y * 53) & 0xFF
                    a = (255 - ((x * 41 + y * 19) & 0xFF))
                    o = x * 4
                    row[o:o+4] = bytes((r, g, b, a))
            rows.append(b"\x00" + bytes(row))  # filter None
        return rows


def _bytes_per_pixel(color_type: int, bit_depth: int) -> int:
    if bit_depth < 8:
        # packed; return ceiling to compute row storage for 8-bit packing in our generator
        if color_type in (0, 3):
            return 1  # not used directly outside _make_rows
        # other combinations with <8 not used here
    if color_type == 0:
        return 1
    if color_type == 2:
        return 3
    if color_type == 3:
        return 1
    if color_type == 4:
        return 2
    if color_type == 6:
        return 4
    return 3


def _build_png(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose image characteristics
    color_type = r.choice([6, 2, 3, 4, 0])  # prioritize RGBA/RGB/Indexed but include GA/Gray
    if color_type in (0, 3):
        bit_depth = r.choice([1, 2, 4, 8])
    else:
        bit_depth = 8

    # small dimensions; vary to exercise row/stride and filters
    width = r.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 31, 32])
    height = r.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 31])

    interlace = r.choice([0, 1])  # enable some interlaced cases

    chunks = [PNG_SIG, _ihdr(width, height, bit_depth, color_type, interlace)]

    # Add color management metadata variants
    cm_choice = r.randrange(5)
    if cm_choice == 0:
        chunks.append(_srgb(r.randrange(4)))
    elif cm_choice == 1:
        # gAMA only
        gamma_vals = [45455, 50000, 100000, 25000]  # ~2.2, 2.0, 1.0, 4.0
        chunks.append(_gama(r.choice(gamma_vals)))
    elif cm_choice == 2:
        # gAMA + cHRM
        chunks.append(_gama(45455))
        # cHRM fixed-point scaled by 100000
        chunks.append(_chrm(31270, 32900, 64000, 33000, 30000, 60000, 15000, 6000))
    elif cm_choice == 3:
        # iCCP minimal profile payload (not a real ICC, but valid chunk structure)
        prof = b"dummy ICC profile" * 4
        chunks.append(_iCCP("Profile", prof))

    # Ancillary tEXt chunk
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        chunks.append(_text("Software", "pnggen-fuzz-seeded"))

    # Palette for indexed
    palette = []
    if color_type == 3:
        palette_size = r.randrange(2, 256)
        for i in range(palette_size):
            palette.append(((i * 97) % 256, (i * 57) % 256, (i * 13) % 256))
        chunks.append(_plte(palette))
        # Optional transparency for a prefix of palette entries
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            alpha_len = r.randrange(1, min(16, palette_size))
            alpha = [(i * 17) % 256 for i in range(alpha_len)]
            chunks.append(_trns_for_palette(alpha))

    # Build pixel rows
    bpp = _bytes_per_pixel(color_type, bit_depth)
    rows = _make_rows(width, height, bpp, color_type, bit_depth)

    # Optionally add filter variety: add a few rows with Sub/Up filters for 8-bit depths
    if bit_depth == 8 and color_type in (2, 4, 6) and len(rows) >= 2 and random.random() < 0.5:
        # Change first row to Sub (1): simple left predictor affects decoding path
        r0 = bytearray(rows[0])
        r0[0] = 1
        rows[0] = bytes(r0)
        # Change second row to Up (2)
        r1 = bytearray(rows[1])
        r1[0] = 2
        rows[1] = bytes(r1)

    chunks.append(_idat_rows(rows))
    chunks.append(_iend())

    png = b"".join(chunks)

    # Ensure under 4096 bytes: if too large, reduce size by adjusting compression level via recompress or shrink dims
    if len(png) > 4096:
        # fallback: rebuild with smaller dims, grayscale
        small_width = 8
        small_height = 8
        ct = 6 if color_type != 3 else 3
        bd = 8 if ct != 3 else 4
        chunks2 = [PNG_SIG, _ihdr(small_width, small_height, bd, ct, 0)]
        if ct == 3:
            pal = [(i, i, i) for i in range(16)]
            chunks2.append(_plte(pal))
        rows2 = _make_rows(small_width, small_height, _bytes_per_pixel(ct, bd), ct, bd)
        chunks2.append(_idat_rows(rows2))
        chunks2.append(_iend())
        png = b"".join(chunks2)

    return png


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Generate a valid PNG image byte stream suitable for rwpng_read_image24 fuzzing.
    The generator creates diverse, valid PNGs across color types, bit depths, interlace,
    and metadata chunks to exercise different decoding paths. Output size <= 4096 bytes.
    """
    return _build_png(seed)

import random
import struct
import zlib

# This generator targets FUZZ_PARAM_STR usage in the rwpng_write_image8 and rwpng_write_image24 stubs.
# The stubs consume the returned byte string cyclically to fill:
# - png8 palette entries (r,g,b,a) and indexed pixel data (palette indices)
# - png24 RGBA pixel data
# Our strategy is to generate compact, structured entropy blocks that produce interesting images:
# - Solid colors, full gradients, checkerboards, stripes
# - Alpha ramps and opaque/transparent toggles
# - Palettes with edge cases (all same color, grayscale ramp, fully transparent, alternating extremes)
# - Short repeating sequences of various lengths to exercise modulo access
# The output is a small byte string (<=4096 bytes) without external dependencies.

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _bytes_from_colors(colors):
    # colors: list of (r,g,b,a) tuples 0..255
    out = bytearray()
    for r, g, b, a in colors:
        out.extend((r & 0xFF, g & 0xFF, b & 0xFF, a & 0xFF))
    return bytes(out)


def _make_palette_pattern(kind: str, seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    colors = []
    if kind == "solid":
        c = (rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256))
        colors = [c] * rnd.randrange(1, 256)
    elif kind == "grayscale_ramp":
        n = rnd.randrange(2, 257)
        for i in range(n):
            v = int(255 * i / max(1, n - 1))
            a = 255
            colors.append((v, v, v, a))
    elif kind == "alpha_ramp":
        n = rnd.randrange(2, 257)
        r = rnd.randrange(256)
        g = rnd.randrange(256)
        b = rnd.randrange(256)
        for i in range(n):
            a = int(255 * i / max(1, n - 1))
            colors.append((r, g, b, a))
    elif kind == "alternating_extremes":
        n = rnd.randrange(2, 257)
        c1 = (0, 0, 0, 0)
        c2 = (255, 255, 255, 255)
        for i in range(n):
            colors.append(c1 if (i % 2 == 0) else c2)
    elif kind == "random_palette":
        n = rnd.randrange(1, 257)
        for _ in range(n):
            colors.append((rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256)))
    elif kind == "pastel_palette":
        n = rnd.randrange(4, 257)
        base = (rnd.randrange(128, 256), rnd.randrange(128, 256), rnd.randrange(128, 256))
        for i in range(n):
            r = min(255, max(0, base[0] + rnd.randrange(-30, 31)))
            g = min(255, max(0, base[1] + rnd.randrange(-30, 31)))
            b = min(255, max(0, base[2] + rnd.randrange(-30, 31)))
            a = 255
            colors.append((r, g, b, a))
    else:
        # Fallback single black
        colors = [(0, 0, 0, 255)]
    return _bytes_from_colors(colors)


def _make_pixel_sequences(kind: str, seed: int, max_len: int = 1024) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    data = bytearray()
    if kind == "solid_index":
        idx = rnd.randrange(256)
        data.extend([idx] * rnd.randrange(1, max_len))
    elif kind == "ramp":
        n = rnd.randrange(2, max_len)
        for i in range(n):
            data.append(i % 256)
    elif kind == "checker":
        n = rnd.randrange(2, max_len)
        a = rnd.randrange(256)
        b = rnd.randrange(256)
        for i in range(n):
            data.append(a if (i % 2 == 0) else b)
    elif kind == "stripes":
        n = rnd.randrange(2, max_len)
        period = rnd.randrange(2, 33)
        palette = [rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(period)]
        for i in range(n):
            data.append(palette[i % period])
    elif kind == "random":
        n = rnd.randrange(1, max_len)
        for _ in range(n):
            data.append(rnd.randrange(256))
    else:
        data.append(0)
    return bytes(data)


def _make_rgba_sequences(kind: str, seed: int, max_len: int = 2048) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    data = bytearray()
    if kind == "solid_rgba":
        rgba = [rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(4)]
        n = rnd.randrange(4, max_len // 4 * 4 + 1)
        if n < 4:
            n = 4
        count = n // 4
        for _ in range(count):
            data.extend(rgba)
    elif kind == "gradient_rgba":
        npx = rnd.randrange(1, max_len // 4 + 1)
        r0, g0, b0, a0 = [rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(4)]
        r1, g1, b1, a1 = [rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(4)]
        for i in range(npx):
            t = i / max(1, npx - 1)
            r = int(r0 + (r1 - r0) * t) & 0xFF
            g = int(g0 + (g1 - g0) * t) & 0xFF
            b = int(b0 + (b1 - b0) * t) & 0xFF
            a = int(a0 + (a1 - a0) * t) & 0xFF
            data.extend((r, g, b, a))
    elif kind == "alpha_toggle":
        npx = rnd.randrange(2, max_len // 4 + 1)
        rgb = [rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(3)]
        for i in range(npx):
            a = 255 if (i % 2 == 0) else 0
            data.extend((rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2], a))
    elif kind == "random":
        n = rnd.randrange(4, max_len)
        for _ in range(n):
            data.append(rnd.randrange(256))
    else:
        data.extend((0, 0, 0, 255))
    return bytes(data)


def _mix_blocks(blocks):
    # Interleave different blocks to create richer entropy cycles
    # while keeping size bounded.
    out = bytearray()
    for b in blocks:
        if not b:
            continue
        out.extend(b)
        if len(out) > MAX_SIZE:
            return bytes(out[:MAX_SIZE])
    return bytes(out[:MAX_SIZE])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide on a theme that will synchronize palette and pixel data in interesting ways.
    palette_kind = rnd.choice([
        "solid",
        "grayscale_ramp",
        "alpha_ramp",
        "alternating_extremes",
        "random_palette",
        "pastel_palette",
    ])
    pixel_kind = rnd.choice([
        "solid_index",
        "ramp",
        "checker",
        "stripes",
        "random",
    ])
    rgba_kind = rnd.choice([
        "solid_rgba",
        "gradient_rgba",
        "alpha_toggle",
        "random",
    ])

    # Create blocks with separate sub-seeds to enhance variability while staying deterministic.
    pal = _make_palette_pattern(palette_kind, seed ^ 0xA5A5_0001)
    idx = _make_pixel_sequences(pixel_kind, seed ^ 0x5A5A_0002, max_len=1536)
    rgba = _make_rgba_sequences(rgba_kind, seed ^ 0x33CC_0003, max_len=3072)

    # Add small headers to encourage diverse short cycles encountered by modulo access.
    # These headers are just entropy; the C++ harness treats the data as raw bytes.
    header = bytearray()
    # 8 bytes from seed, 4 bytes of sizes (capped), and a small marker string.
    header.extend(struct.pack("<Q", (seed & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)))
    header.extend(struct.pack("<III", len(pal) & 0xFFFFFFFF, len(idx) & 0xFFFFFFFF, len(rgba) & 0xFFFFFFFF))
    marker = b"PQEZ"  # arbitrary marker
    header.extend(marker)

    # Optionally compress one block and include both raw and compressed to provide different byte distributions.
    # Still valid as entropy bytes.
    if rnd.random() < 0.5 and len(rgba) > 16:
        try:
            comp = zlib.compress(rgba, level=rnd.randrange(1, 10))
            if len(comp) < len(rgba) and len(comp) < 1024:
                rgba = comp
        except Exception:
            pass

    # Interleave to keep within budget and yield variety for both palettes and pixels.
    blocks = [bytes(header), pal, idx, rgba]
    out = _mix_blocks(blocks)

    # Ensure non-empty, as the harness replaces empty with "\x00" and that reduces variety.
    if not out:
        out = b"\x00"

    # Cap size.
    if len(out) > MAX_SIZE:
        out = out[:MAX_SIZE]

    return out
